angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 484,903 km at 58.41 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 17.1212 +/- 0.0213 mas (same row, RUWE 1.14): 58.41 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.697 +/- 0.005 solar radii from Borsato et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1130 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...689A..52B/abstract): 484,903 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.745 +/- 0.007 solar masses from Borsato et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1130 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...689A..52B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4360 +/- 108 K from Borsato et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1130 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...689A..52B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Borsato et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1130 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...689A..52B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1130.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.624, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
